evidence.paraphrase: The report assesses whether the banking system remains able to support economic activity while maintaining safety and soundness.
CET1 capital, liquidity, profitability, loan growth, delinquencies, charge-offs, commercial real-estate exposure, market leverage, and CDS spreads are defined as complementary condition indicators.
Aggregate resilience is evaluated alongside pockets of deterioration and bank-size heterogeneity; strong averages do not erase concentration or borrower-quality risk.
Supervisory aggregates mix bank populations and accounting conventions, so MacroTrace must expose bank-size composition and must not infer economy-wide credit supply from one capital ratio.

executive_summary: The June 2026 Supervision and Regulation Report turns U.S. banking conditions into a balance-sheet monitoring workflow: capital adequacy, liquidity, profitability, loan growth, delinquency and charge-offs, market risk indicators, and commercial real-estate concentration. Regulatory material is context; the reusable macro content is the credit-supply and bank-resilience path, with separate large-bank and community/regional-bank cuts.

method_routes.aggregation_role: financial-sector resilience node feeding credit and downside-risk lanes
method_routes.estimand: direction and breadth of bank resilience and its capacity to sustain credit supply
method_routes.formula: bank_state = registered synthesis(capital, liquidity, earnings, asset quality, market indicators) by bank-size stratum
method_routes.identification_strategy: descriptive bank-condition monitoring; causal credit-supply effects require a separate bank-level panel design
identifying_assumptions: bank population and accounting definitions are stable or reconciled
capital and asset-quality indicators are lag-aligned
aggregate results are stratified by bank size and exposure
method_routes.method_family: bank balance-sheet condition panel with size-stratified monitoring
robustness_requirements: market CDS versus accounting asset quality
method_routes.sample_definition: U.S. regulatory and market data for insured banks and large banking organizations through the report cutoff

questions.horizon_text: current banking conditions and near-term resilience
questions.question_text: Are U.S. banks sufficiently capitalized, liquid, and profitable to sustain credit supply, and where are asset-quality or concentration risks increasing?
